records.claim: Opportunity is a robotic rover that was active on Mars from 2004 until 2018.
records.passage: Opportunity, also known as MER-B (Mars Exploration Rover – B) or MER-1, and nicknamed Oppy, is a robotic rover that was active on Mars from 2004 until 2018.

records.claim: Opportunity was operational on Mars for 5111 sols (14 years, 138 days on Earth).
records.passage: Opportunity was operational on Mars for 5111 sols (14 years, 138 days on Earth).

records.claim: This careful operation allowed Opportunity to operate for 57 times its designed lifespan.
records.passage: This careful operation allowed Opportunity to operate for 57 times its designed lifespan, exceeding the initial plan by 14 years, 47 days (in Earth time).

records.claim: Mission highlights included the initial 90-sol mission, finding meteorites, and over two years of exploring and studying Victoria crater.
records.passage: Mission highlights included the initial 90-sol mission, finding meteorites such as Heat Shield Rock (Meridiani Planum meteorite), and over two years of exploring and studying Victoria crater.

narration.text: Why a 90-sol rover kept going 14 years.
Opportunity lasted 57 times its designed lifespan.
It stayed active on Mars from 2004 all the way to 2018.
Winds sometimes cleaned dust off its solar panels.
In 2018, a planet-wide dust storm starved it of power.
So careful engineering can outlast every plan.
